title: fix(core,components): an update's Undo covers its named declaration's `patch`, and no action renderer forwards a row `patch` (objectui#13022)
body:
Fixes #13022

Clause-②: no

An `operation: 'update'` action's Undo snapshot now covers the `patch` of the declared action its `name` names, plus the collected params. No action renderer forwards a page action row's own `patch` any more.

This is the runner-and-renderer half of the card. The published-input half is pin-coupled and rides objectui#12971: the `patch` input that `action:button` and `action:icon` publish, `action-button-icon-inputs-11168.test.tsx`'s input list, and `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`. At today's pin (`@objectstack/spec` 18.0.0-next.3) the spec still declares the row `patch`, and the parity test's reverse direction requires the input. **This PR goes ready only after objectui#12971 lands and this branch has merged `main`.**

## Why

objectstack-ai/objectstack#24442 (`69f342b924`) retires a page action row's own `patch` in `@objectstack/spec` 18, on `action:button`, `action:icon` and the `action:group` / `action:menu` member. A row's `operation: 'update'` runs the declared action its `name` names. The platform action route resolves that declaration by name and writes the declaration's `patch` under the params it is sent. The row's own `patch` has reached no request since objectui#12941 (PR #12944). The runner read it for the Undo snapshot only, so the snapshot covered the wrong fields. Once no row carries a `patch`, a row's snapshot covered the collected params and missed the fields the route wrote.

## What changed

- `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`
  - New `declaredUpdatePatch(action, context, objectName)`. It reads the `patch` of the declaration the action's `name` names from the `objectActions` the host publishes for the dispatch's object (new `readContextObjectActions`). It is scoped like `readContextObjectFields`: only the context's own object.
  - When the host published no list for that object, or the list does not name the action, it reads the def's own `patch`. A host that dispatches an object's action whole hands that in: `ObjectGrid` rows, `DeclaredActionsBar`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge` and `page:header`.
  - `executeUpdateOperation` builds `written` from that `patch`, which gives `writtenFields` and `redoData`. The request is unchanged: `{ ...action, params: { ...collected } }`.
  - A nameless action skips the lookup.
  - The `ActionDef.patch` and method docs say what the key is now.
- `useConsoleActionRuntime` and `RecordDetailView` publish `objectActions: objectDef.actions` in the runner context, beside `objectFields`.
- `action-button.tsx`, `action-icon.tsx`, `action-group.tsx` and `action-menu.tsx` drop `patch: schema.patch` / `patch: action.patch` and the comments that described the forward. `operation` is still forwarded.
- `scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` gets four `JUSTIFIED` entries, `action:button:patch` and the three siblings (issue 13022). Without them the gate reds, because the runner still reads `action.patch` off a whole-dispatched declaration. The entry says why the omission is correct.
- `predicate-fields.ts`: doc only (see "Premise" below).
- Docs: `packages/core/README.md` gains "Which fields an `operation: 'update'` Undo covers", which documents the host's `objectActions`. `content/docs/guide/layout.md` no longer lists `patch` among the forwarded keys and says the node runs its named declaration.
- `.changeset/13022-action-row-declared-patch.md`: patch for `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/components` and `@object-ui/app-shell`.

## Call graph used (dispatch Zone 2, item 2)

The declaration was **not** in hand at the capture site. A page row reaches `executeUpdateOperation` as the def the renderer composes from the node. `action:bar` draws a declared action through the same `action:button` / `action:menu` renderers, and a spread-based host hands the declaration itself. The runner context held `objectName` and `objectFields` only.

The shortest thread mirrors objectui#11122's `objectFields`. The hosts' `objectDef.actions` (the list the route resolves names against) goes into the context, then through `ActionProvider` to `new ActionRunner(context)`, then `execute`, then `executeUpdateOperation`, then `declaredUpdatePatch`. That puts it next to `captureUpdateUndoData` at the capture site.

## Premise (dispatch Zone 1 and Zone 2, measured on `origin/main` `47508f3b`)

- **`undoableWrittenKeys` (predicate-fields) does not read a row.** Its inputs are `listViewPredicates`' `rowActionDefs` (the host-resolved row defs), `bulkActionDefs` and `objectActions`. All of them are definitions their writer applies whole, and no page action row reaches it. So it already reads the declared `patch` that the `$select` harvest owes the row. Only its doc changed, to say so. The runner change reads the same declarations on the console hosts.
- **Item 1, the request body is unchanged.** `action-row-declared-patch-13022.test.tsx` has the test "the request a row sends carries no field value, with or without a `patch` on the row". It asserts `{ recordId: 't1', params: {} }` through the real `createServerActionHandler`. It stays green with the forward put back (ablation 2 below), so dropping the forward moves no request byte. `action-button-undoable-11168` "on a record page" pins the same body.
- **Item 3, a nameless `operation: 'update'` row today.** Measured with a throwaway probe through the real runner and `createServerActionHandler` (not committed). The answer is `{ success: false, error: 'Action has no name — a server action must declare one' }`, with 0 requests and an error toast, and the action never reaches the Undo capture. Unchanged here.

## Tests (union after the final commit, head `a5cd587d`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over `packages/core/src/actions/`, `predicate-fields.test.ts`, `packages/components/src/renderers/action/`, every `useConsoleActionRuntime*` test, nine `RecordDetailView` action/undo tests, both `AppContent.undo*` tests, `plugin-grid` `undoProjectedRow-10404`, `plugin-form` `affordanceGrantMap-12082`, both `check-action-forward-parity` script suites and `apps/console` `registry-inputs-spec-parity` / `public-block-binding-reach` / `public-contract`. Result: **102 files, 1761 tests passed**.
- New `ActionRunner.declaredPatch-13022.test.ts` (core, 7 tests) covers:
  - the declaration's `patch` is snapshotted for a row with none;
  - the declaration wins over a def's own `patch`;
  - a declaration with no `patch` gives a params-only snapshot;
  - a written field the row lacks gives no Undo, with the warning;
  - with no published list, a whole-dispatched declaration is read whole;
  - a dispatch to another object does not read this object's list;
  - control: no `patch` and no list gives no Undo.
- New `action-row-declared-patch-13022.test.tsx` (components, 9 tests) covers:
  - each of the four surfaces hands the runner `operation` and no `patch`;
  - the request body, with and without a row `patch`;
  - Undo covers the named declaration's `patch`, plus a collected param;
  - a row's own `patch` is never covered;
  - control: a host with no list gives a patch-only row no Undo.
- Updated pins:
  - `action-forward-precedence.test.tsx`: `patch` leaves both key-order lists.
  - `action-button-icon-inputs-11168.test.tsx`, the `operation: update` case only: the def carries `operation` and no `patch`.
  - `action-button-undoable-11168.test.tsx`: the host publishes the declarations, and the rows carry no `patch`.

## Ablation (both legs through `objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, on committed `9f41095f`)

1. **The snapshot change.**
   - Mutation: `const patch = declaredUpdatePatch(action, this.context, objectName);` became `const patch = patchMembers(action.patch);`, the pre-change read.
   - On disk: anchor 1 to 0, blob `79aef211708b` to `1cb9d3ac99ea`.
   - Expected red; observed red: **6 failed / 10 passed of 16**. They are the 3 core and 3 components Undo cases above. The request-body, no-forward, cross-object and control cases stayed green.
   - Restored: blob back to `79aef211708b`, equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, and the rerun gave 16/16.
2. **The renderer forward.**
   - Mutation: `patch: schema.patch,` put back into `action:button`'s forward.
   - The first attempt was refused by the tool, because the replacement contained the anchor. Nothing ran, and the file was restored. It was re-run with a two-line anchor.
   - On disk: anchor 1 to 0, blob `70dbbd6e83d5` to `c825cec7358a`.
   - Expected red; observed red: **3 failed / 14 passed of 17**: the two `action:button` key-order pins and "action:button hands the runner `operation` and no `patch`". The request-body pin stayed green, which is item 1. "the `patch` a row carries itself is never covered" also stayed green, because the published declaration wins in the runner as well.
   - Restored: blob `70dbbd6e83d5` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

No build or `dist` leg: the tests import `../ActionRunner` relatively, and vitest aliases `@object-ui/core` to `src`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The residual direction, not changed here.** A host that publishes no declarations for the dispatch's object reads the def's own `patch`. A row carries none, so a row on such a host keeps today's params-only snapshot. Two cases reach it:
  - a page row under a runtime with no bound object, such as `PageView`, whose runtime binds no `objectName`;
  - a row whose `objectName` names an object other than the host's.

  Both console record surfaces, `ObjectView` and `DeclaredActionsBar` publish. Making "no declaration found" refuse Undo instead would also refuse it for every whole-dispatched param-only action on such a host. The seat may want that ruled; it is in the report.
- **Between this PR and objectui#12971**, `action:button` / `action:icon` still publish a `patch` input that the block no longer forwards. The spec at today's pin still declares it, and objectui#12971 removes it with the pin bump.
- `objectActions` rides `ActionProvider`'s `JSON.stringify(context)` memo key, beside `objectFields`.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
